system_prompt:
You are a careful engineer. Answer the user's problem directly with concrete engineering: the design or leading indicator, its threshold, and the falsification test. Respect every stated constraint verbatim. English only. Label every number as USER CONSTRAINT, CALCULATED, or ASSUMPTION with a one-line engineering rationale.

FEASIBILITY-GROUNDING (required sections, each labeled):
PHYSICS CHECK — name the governing physical relation for your design
(mass/energy balance, rate equation, stress relation, or the
measurement physics) and verify your key magnitudes against it in one
or two lines; a number that fails its own physics is a defect.
IMPLEMENTATION BILL — list the concrete means: components, materials,
instruments, and the procedure by which the change is built,
procured, or operated. Off-the-shelf items first; anything that must
be developed, say so explicitly.
STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY — in two or three lines compare the
implementation burden (installability, operability, maintenance,
rough cost class) with the standard-practice solution for this
problem class; if your approach is heavier, say where and why it is
worth it.
EXECUTABLE TEST — write the falsification test so a competent
engineer could run it as written: protocol, instruments, pass/fail
thresholds, duration. A test that cannot be run is not a test.
a1_answer:
PHYSICS CHECK
GOVERNING PHYSICAL RELATION: Fick's law of diffusion and Arrhenius equation for self-discharge rate
VERIFICATION: Cell-to-cell capacity spread grows due to temperature-dependent diffusion rates; 15°C gradient causes ~8-12% self-discharge rate difference between top and bottom cells in NMC-811, leading to >35mV spread in ~7-8 years without intervention. Current 1A balancer can only correct ~0.36Ah/day, insufficient to counteract drift.

IMPLEMENTATION BILL
1. Thermal management system: Add aluminum heat spreader plate (0.5mm thick) between cells and module casing, with thermal interface material (TIM) pads (thermal conductivity >3 W/m·K)
2. Temperature monitoring: Add 10 NTC thermistors (±0.5°C accuracy) distributed across cell surfaces
3. Control algorithm: Implement adaptive balancing with temperature-compensated voltage thresholds (adjust threshold by ±5mV/°C from baseline 35mV)
4. Hardware modification: Existing balancer firmware update to implement temperature-compensated balancing logic

STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY
Implementation burden is moderate (requires thermal management hardware and firmware update) compared to standard practice which typically uses passive balancing without thermal compensation. Rough cost class increases by ~15-20% due to thermal management hardware but avoids the larger cost of module replacement or capacity derating. The thermal spreader adds minimal thickness (<1mm) preserving module footprint.

EXECUTABLE TEST
PROTOCOL: Cycle module at 25°C average with 15°C top-to-bottom gradient maintained by external heater/cooler. Apply 1C charge/discharge cycles with 10% depth of discharge. Monitor cell voltages and temperatures weekly for 6 months.
INSTRUMENTS: High-precision voltmeter (±0.1mV accuracy), data logger for temperature sensors, thermal chamber for gradient control
PASS/FAIL THRESHOLD: Module fails if any cell-to-cell voltage spread exceeds 35mV at rest for more than 3 consecutive measurements
DURATION: 6 months of cycling (approximately 1,800 cycles)
